guideline: Score it a 1 when the translation has nothing to do with the source; or when the translation has many unknown words; or when the translation looks like word salad. ... Score it a 6 when the translation is perfect in every sense of the word - something a professional translator/interpreter would come up with when she understands well the context in which the source sentence was produced.

Scoring rubric: 1 = completely unrelated or nonsensical; 2 = meaning lost; 3 = meaning partially transferred; 4 = meaning generally preserved but mechanical with errors; 5 = meaning fully preserved, no grammatical errors but not fully natural; 6 = perfect translation as a professional would produce.

The annotators are asked to judge the translation on a scale of 1 to 6, following the guidelines outlined in the following scoring rubric. They can assign scores in increments of 0.2, allowing for more detailed assessments, such as 1.2, 1.4, and so on.
